items.title: Ajeet Bharti bail plea: Delhi High Court sees intense exchange between Advocate Jai Dehadrai and judge
items.summary: The hearing of YouTuber Ajeet Bharti’s anticipatory bail plea before the Delhi High Court saw some tense moments between Bharti’s counsel, Jai Anant Dehadrai and Justice Saurabh Banerjee , the judge hearing the case. It started when Dehadrai tried to hand over to the court a document containing the extracted transcript of the allegedly offending remarks made by Bharti in his YouTube video. Justice Banerjee objected to it. He said that Dehadrai could not hand over the words used by Bharti to a court of law. The judge then warned that he would issue a contempt of court notice to Dehadrai. “You cannot hand over the words used by him to a court of law. I will issue contempt notice to you. Phraseology used is not offensive according to you? Please be aware of what you are doing. It contains word which are...You can't hand over those things to the court of law. You should not, as a counsel, hand over this,” Justice Banerjee said. Justice Saurabh Banerjee, Advocate Jai Anant Dehadrai Dehadrai replied that the document merely contained a transcript of what had been alleged in the FIR and was being presented to assist the Court. He said that handing over such documents was a usual practice.

items.title: Private players should not replicate ISRO’s efforts: G Madhavan Nair writes
items.summary: India is at an important transition point in its space programme. The country is moving from a predominantly government-led space programme to an ecosystem in which private companies and startups can participate across the entire value chain. Indian Space Policy 2023 explicitly enables private entities to undertake activities including satellite realisation and operations, launch services, data acquisition and dissemination and ground infrastructure. ​The number of registered space startups has risen from one in 2014 to approximately 440 in 2026​, the government told the Rajya Sabha in August. The government also estimates India’s space economy at approximately US$9 billion in 2026, and predicts this will multiply to US$40–45 billion over the next decade. The question therefore is not whether India should encourage private participation in the space sector – the answer is obvious.
